name: אֱנוֹשׁ
summary: The son of Seth and grandson of Adam, born when Seth was 105; he begot Kenan at ninety and died at 905 (Gen 5:6–11). He stands third in the line from Adam (1Ch 1:1) and in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus, “son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God” (Luk 3:38). The name is the noun אֱנוֹשׁ, “man”, the word scripture uses of man as frail and dying (Psa 103:15; Isa 51:12): as Adam’s name is “man” (אָדָם), so is his grandson’s. Scripture gives no reason for the name, but joins to his birth the notice, “then it was begun to call on the name of Yahweh” (Gen 4:26).

evidence.note: “To Seth also a son was born, and he called his name אֱנוֹשׁ. Then it was begun to call on the name of Yahweh.”
Seth lived 105 years and begot Enosh, and after that 807 years.
Enosh lived ninety years and begot Kenan; “all the days of Enosh were 905 years, and he died”.
Ἐνώς in the genealogy of Jesus; the Peshitta writes אַנוֹשׁ.
The noun the name is: אֱנוֹשׁ כֶּחָצִיר יָמָיו, “man, his days are like grass”.
מָה־אֱנוֹשׁ, “what is man, that you remember him?”

note: The name and the noun are spelled alike, so BDB’s a.ep.ac (40 tokens) counts the noun’s tokens too; only Gen 4:26; 5:6, 7, 9, 10, 11 and 1Ch 1:1 (seven) are the name. The Septuagint writes Ενως and the New Testament Ἐνώς. Gen 5:7’s figure (807 years) is from the Hebrew text as the database has it; check the verse if the summary’s ages are edited. Gen 4:26b is read “then it was begun to call on the name of Yahweh” (הוּחַל, hophal of חלל); the summary does not say who began or what the calling was.
